jobs.excerpt: The Role: A Curious “Hunter” Ready to GrowWe are looking for a Business Development Representative (BDR) who is energized by building new relationships, motivated by meaningful work, and excited to grow a career in sales.
jobs.description:
The Role: A Curious “Hunter” Ready to Grow

We are looking for a Business Development Representative (BDR) who is energized by building new relationships, motivated by meaningful work, and excited to grow a career in sales.

This is an opportunity to develop both outbound prospecting and inbound sales skills while helping healthcare organizations discover language access solutions that improve patient care.

Approximately 60% of your time will be focused on proactively building new pipeline through outbound prospecting, while 40% will be spent managing inbound inquiries, qualifying opportunities, and helping prospective clients take the next step.

If you’re naturally curious, resilient, coachable, and excited by the challenge of opening doors, this role offers an incredible opportunity to learn, grow, and make an impact.

Position Summary

The Business Development Representative (BDR) is responsible for generating qualified sales opportunities through a combination of outbound prospecting and inbound lead management.

As the first point of contact for prospective clients, you’ll introduce hospitals, health systems, clinics, and health insurance organizations to Linguava’s language access solutions—including our on-demand interpretation services (On-Site, Video Remote Interpreting, and Over-the-Phone Interpreting) and our technology platform.

Success in this role comes from balancing proactive outreach with responsive lead management, maintaining a healthy sales pipeline, and consistently creating qualified meetings for our Business Development team. This role serves as an excellent foundation for someone looking to build a long-term career in business development and healthcare sales.

What You’ll Do

Build New Business Opportunities (Approximately 60%)

  • Identify and prospect hospitals, health systems, clinics, and payer organizations across existing and new markets
  • Research target accounts and identify key decision-makers within Language Access, Procurement, Operations, Diversity & Inclusion, and Executive Leadership
  • Execute strategic outbound outreach through phone, email, LinkedIn, and other prospecting channels
  • Develop personalized outreach strategies that generate qualified meetings and build early-stage relationships
  • Expand Linguava’s presence as we continue to grow beyond the Pacific Northwest

Manage & Qualify Inbound Opportunities (Approximately 40%)

  • Respond promptly to inbound inquiries from prospective clients
  • Conduct discovery conversations to understand client needs and qualify opportunities
  • Build relationships with inbound prospects while identifying opportunities to expand conversations and cross-sell additional Linguava services
  • Partner closely with Business Development Managers to ensure seamless handoffs of qualified opportunities
  • Deliver an exceptional first impression of Linguava in every client interaction

Manage Pipeline & Performance

  • Maintain accurate prospect activity, notes, and pipeline data within HubSpot
  • Consistently achieve outreach, follow-up, and qualified meeting goals
  • Develop daily and weekly activity plans to maintain a healthy pipeline
  • Share prospect feedback, market insights, and competitive intelligence with Sales leadership
  • Continuously refine prospecting strategies based on performance and coaching

Who You Are

The Hunter-in-Training

You enjoy opening doors, creating opportunities, and aren’t discouraged by hearing “no.” Every conversation is an opportunity to learn and improve.

The Relationship Builder

Whether someone reaches out to us or you’re making the first call, you know how to build trust, ask thoughtful questions, and create positive first impressions.

The Curious Learner

You’re coachable, eager to learn, and excited to develop your business development and sales skills. You welcome feedback and are motivated by continuous growth.

The Goal Chaser

You enjoy working toward measurable goals and take pride in achieving results. You’re competitive in a healthy way and motivated by creating opportunities through your own effort.

The Strategic Thinker

You don’t rely on mass outreach alone—you research accounts, understand your audience, and personalize your approach to stand out.

The Team Player

You recognize that every qualified meeting contributes to the team’s success and enjoy collaborating with teammates to achieve shared goals.

Required Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • 1–3 years of experience in business development, sales development, lead generation, customer-facing sales, or outbound prospecting
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Experience using HubSpot or a similar CRM platform
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience selling into healthcare organizations or healthcare-related industries
  • Familiarity with language services, healthcare technology, SaaS, or healthcare operations
  • Experience prospecting into enterprise or multi-stakeholder organizations
  • Proven success meeting activity, pipeline generation, or appointment-setting goals

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Salary: $60,000–$75,000 annually, depending on experience, qualifications, and internal equity
  • Variable Compensation: Eligible to earn additional incentive compensation based on qualified meetings scheduled and contribution to pipeline growth
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, and long-term disability insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid Time Off (PTO)
  • Paid Holidays
  • Floating Holiday
  • Volunteer Time Off (VTO)

How You’ll Embody Our Values

People First

You build authentic relationships and create positive experiences with every prospective client.

Doing the Right Thing

You represent Linguava with honesty, integrity, and professionalism in every interaction.

Pursuit of Progress

You embrace coaching, continuously improve your skills, and look for new ways to create opportunities.

Above & Beyond Service

You go the extra mile to understand client needs and create meaningful first impressions.

Have Each Other’s Back

You collaborate closely with Marketing, Business Development, and Client Success to ensure every opportunity has the best chance of becoming a successful partnership.

Why Linguava?

At Linguava, we believe language should never be a barrier to quality healthcare. Every conversation you start has the potential to help healthcare organizations improve communication, advance health equity, and better serve patients with limited English proficiency.

We’re building a collaborative, mission-driven team where people are encouraged to learn, grow, and take on new challenges. This role is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a long-term career in business development. You’ll receive coaching, mentorship, and hands-on experience in both outbound prospecting and inbound sales while working alongside experienced leaders in healthcare and language access.

If you’re hungry to learn, motivated by meaningful work, and excited to grow your career, we’d love to hear from you.

Our Interview Process

We believe interviews are a two-way conversation. Our goal is to help you learn more about Linguava while giving us the opportunity to get to know you and your experience.

Our hiring process for this role includes:

  1. Phone Screen with our Director of Human Resources

  2. Video Interview with the Hiring Manager

  3. Final Interview with members of our Sales Leadership team

Throughout the process, we’ll keep you informed about next steps and provide updates as decisions are made. We know your time is valuable and are committed to providing a thoughtful, transparent, and respectful hiring experience from application through offer.

Linguava is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating an inclusive workplace that reflects the communities we serve.

You will work across frontend, backend, cloud, and data layers to deliver high-quality software solutions and improve operational efficiency.

You will collaborate with product owners, architects, business stakeholders, infrastructure teams, and fellow engineers to translate business requirements into scalable and maintainable applications. The ideal candidate is a hands-on engineer with strong experience in modern frontend frameworks, backend development, cloud platforms, API development, and software engineering best practices.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, test, and maintain full stack applications using modern frontend and backend technologies.
  • Develop responsive and user-friendly web applications using React, Angular, JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
  • Build scalable backend APIs, services, and microservices using technologies such as Java, Spring Boot, Python, .NET, Node.js, or similar frameworks.
  • Design and implement integrations between enterprise platforms, internal applications, cloud services, databases, and third-party systems.

jobs.description:
Highlights:

Location: Portugal

Language: Fluent in Russian and English (C1+)

About Fundraise Up

We’re Fundraise Up - a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless, and accessible to all. Every month, our technology powers tens of millions of dollars in donations across the globe. We focus on innovation that directly impacts results: faster load times, higher conversion rates, global payment support, and accessibility-first design.

Our platform is trusted by many of the world’s leading nonprofits, including UNICEF, the Alzheimer’s Association, and a wide range of global NGOs. With a 4.9/5 rating across top software review platforms, we’re recognized not just for our impact - but for the quality of the product we deliver.

A Truly Global Product

We operate in the enterprise segment, serving nonprofit organizations across North America, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Europe.

We’re building a large and complex product ecosystem that serves nonprofits, donors, and partners around the world. The platform includes a modern checkout experience and customizable widgets (each a standalone SPA), donor, organization, and partner portals, admin tools, and several internal apps.

The Team

We are a distributed team of 160+ product professionals. Our team members are mainly based across Spain, Poland, Portugal, Georgia, Armenia, Serbia, Turkey, and Cyprus.

Despite our scale, we operate like a focused team - where every task matters and every voice is heard. We value thoughtful collaboration, strong engineering practices, and a product mindset. You’ll be joining a team where quality, mentorship, and mutual respect come first.

About In-Person Giving at Fundraise Up

In-Person Giving brings the quality and connected data of Fundraise Up’s online donation experience into physical fundraising moments.

The product begins with Tap to Donate and Giving Station: staff-led and self-service experiences that let nonprofits accept contactless donations at events, in public spaces, and through other offline workflows. Every transaction should connect to the same campaigns, donor records, reporting, CRM integrations, and operational controls used across Fundraise Up.

The next product direction is Events & Commerce. It includes ticket sales, check-in, merchandise and food purchases, symbolic purchases, auctions, paddle raises, and additional donations before and during an event. These capabilities must work as one connected fundraising system rather than another isolated event tool.

About the Role

We are hiring a Product Manager to own Events & Commerce within the broader In-Person Giving product line.

This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn a large category into a focused product direction grounded in customer workflows, live usage, and commercial evidence.

You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader In-Person Giving area so that event commerce builds on the same payment, campaign, donor-data, reporting, mobile, and operational foundations as Tap to Donate and Giving Station. You will also partner with the Peer-to-Peer team where ticketing and event capabilities should be shared rather than rebuilt separately.

This is not an event-planning, sales, or internal project-coordination role.

What You’ll Own

Define the product direction

  • Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear Events & Commerce product thesis and sequenced roadmap.
  • Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to replace every event platform at once.
  • Decide which capabilities belong in the shared In-Person Giving foundation and which require an Events-specific model.
  • Make explicit decisions about what Fundraise Up should build, integrate, partner on, or deliberately exclude.
  • Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions visible.

Lead discovery and product definition

  • Work directly with nonprofit fundraising teams, event operators, finance teams, volunteers, attendees, donors, design partners, and internal GTM teams.
  • Map the complete workflow before, during, and after an event—including purchase, donation, check-in, fulfillment, reconciliation, reporting, and follow-up.
  • Validate decisions through interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, and live product usage.
  • Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and expectations created by incumbent event platforms.
  • Shape problems such as ticket sales, QR-based check-in, guest management, commerce catalogues, FMV and receipts, on-site purchases, auctions, paddle raises, refunds, attribution, reporting, and integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist.

Shape and deliver the product

  • Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration.
  • Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, state transitions, and decision records.
  • Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, QA, and GTM partners.
  • Design for real event conditions: staff and volunteer operators, self-service flows, mobile devices, optional hardware, unreliable connectivity, high-volume moments, and operational recovery.
  • Ensure that event capabilities reuse Fundraise Up’s existing payments, campaign, donor, reporting, CRM, and identity infrastructure wherever possible.
  • Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early.

Launch, learn, and drive outcomes

  • Launch through EAPs with clear entry criteria, target workflows, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas.
  • Understand whether organizations can configure and run the target event workflows without heavy manual work or disconnected tools.
  • Measure whether attendees can purchase, check in, donate, and receive the right confirmation or receipt through a clear experience.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, Support, Finance, Legal, and Operations on positioning, commitments, enablement, and launch readiness.
  • Connect product evidence to activation, adoption, event completion, GPV, expansion, pipeline, retention, and operational cost.
  • Turn evidence into explicit recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, partner, or stop.

Work AI-native

  • Use AI for research synthesis, workflow analysis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation.
  • Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment.

Requirements

  • 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company.
  • End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design.
  • Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs.
  • Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions.
  • Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records.
  • Ability to work with transactional, multi-actor workflows involving permissions, states, money, and data relationships.
  • High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English.

Strong plus

  • Experience with ticketing, event technology, commerce, POS, payments, marketplaces, registration, auctions, or other transaction-heavy products.
  • Experience with mobile applications, contactless payments, physical devices, or hardware-enabled workflows.
  • Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, nonprofits, or other operationally complex customer environments.
  • Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP.
  • Knowledge of CRM integrations, financial reconciliation, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL.
  • Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations.

This Role May Not Be a Fit If

  • You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership.
  • You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built.
  • You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration.
  • You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment.
  • You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward.
  • You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes.

Why work with us

  • Build a new product direction from research through live customer use.
  • Work in a large, proven fundraising category with clear customer demand and meaningful commercial potential.
  • Shape ticketing and event commerce as part of a broader fundraising platform rather than an isolated event tool.
  • Work with real nonprofit customers, rich product evidence, and experienced cross-functional partners.
  • Join a small team where product managers have meaningful ownership and direct access to Product leadership.
  • Help define an AI-native approach to product management in practice.
  • Build technology that helps nonprofits engage more supporters and raise more money for their missions.

Compensation

  • The compensation range for this role is €5,200 - €5,700 gross.
  • Final compensation will be determined based on relevant experience, skills, qualifications, alignment with the role’s requirements and location.

Benefits

  • Private medical insurance for the employee and their family
  • 22 paid vacation days per year
  • Up to 14 paid public holidays per year
  • 5 company-paid sick leave days
  • English learning courses.
  • Relevant professional education.
  • Gym or swimming pool.
  • Home Office Setup Assistance: the company offers assistance with purchasing furniture (office chair, office desk, monitor) and other items to create a comfortable workspace.
  • Co-working.
  • Remote working.

jobs.description:
Daymark Health is a value-based oncology company redefining the cancer care experience for patients, providers, and health plans. Daymark’s comprehensive, personalized cancer care platform empowers patients with dedicated care navigation, symptom-focused support, behavioral health care, and social resources. Combined with evidence-based health interventions and a hybrid in-person + virtual care model, Daymark is improving the overall cancer experience for patients, providers, and health plans – and setting a new standard in cancer care.

Daymark’s groundbreaking approach is led by CEO Dr. Justin Bekelman, a pioneer in transforming cancer care, alongside some of the nation’s foremost leaders in oncology and value-based care. Daymark Health is backed by Maverick Ventures, Yosemite, Oncology Ventures, Healthier Capital, Blue Venture Fund, and Healthcare Foundry.

Be cautious of recruitment fraud, and always confirm that communications are coming from an official Daymark Health email.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for someone to take ownership of Licensing and Credentialing at Daymark and grow it into a real function. You’ll be responsible for keeping our clinicians licensed and credentialed to practice and bill as we move into new states quickly, covering licensing strategy, commercial payer credentialing, Medicare enrollment, and the compliance questions that sit underneath all of it. The work touches Clinical Operations, Finance, Legal, Revenue Cycle, and People, so you’ll be comfortable operating across all of them.

This is a role for someone who is genuinely hands-on with licensing and credentialing. You know the compacts, the expedited routes, and how to time credentialing against launch and payer-contracting deadlines, but you can also step back and think about state expansion and prescriptive authority as connected problems. We think of this as the level where execution and strategy meet: detailed enough to run the applications and renewals yourself today, senior enough to design the system and, over time, hire and lead a team of specialists to run it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Clinical Licensing Strategy & Execution

  • Set the multi-state licensing roadmap and priorities against Daymark’s launch timeline, and know the terrain state by state for MD, DO, NP, and RN pathways.
  • Get providers licensed faster by working the fastest route available — interstate compacts (IMLC, NLC, APRN Compact) and FCVS where they apply.
  • Run applications and renewals to completion, from verifications and board back-and-forth through clearing whatever holds them up.
  • Keep the licensing tracker and platform accurate, and keep leadership current on where every provider stands.

Payer Credentialing Strategy, Research & Execution

  • Build the credentialing plan around which payers matter in which states, and time it to line up with licensing and go-live dates.
  • Stand up and maintain CAQH profiles and attestations.
  • Submit and shepherd commercial payer applications, chasing down pending items and fixing whatever the payer flags.
  • Keep the credentialing tracker current and leadership in the loop.

Medicare Credentialing & Enrollment

  • Figure out the Medicare enrollment approach and the right MAC jurisdiction for each state we enter.

jobs.description:
Senior Platform Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure

Type: Remote
Coverage: Pacific Hours (8:00 AM – 5:00 PM PST)

Job Description:

We are looking for a senior engineer to build and operate the cloud-native platform that our products run on. This is a hands-on infrastructure engineering role: you will design and run production Kubernetes platforms, write and maintain the Go services and controllers that extend them, and own the reliability of systems that other engineering teams depend on.

The work spans platform architecture, networking, observability, and production operations. You will write real code: Go services, Kubernetes controllers, custom middleware, but the value you create is measured in platform capability and reliability, not lines shipped. We are looking for someone who is comfortable owning ambiguous, multi-quarter initiatives and driving them to production.

Key Responsibilities:

Platform and Kubernetes Engineering:

  • Design, build, and operate production Kubernetes clusters, including cluster networking, workload isolation, and multi-region topologies.

  • Work with Kubernetes internals: resource quota management, scheduling and cluster behaviour, NetworkPolicy enforcement, and custom controllers or operators.

  • Implement and operate service mesh capabilities: mTLS between services, service-account-level authentication and authorisation, and traffic management across internal and external request paths.

  • Optimise containerised workloads for performance, cost, and resource efficiency.

Software Development in Go, Python or Java:

  • Write, refactor, and maintain production services, controllers, and middleware that extend the platform.

  • Read and contribute to complex existing codebases, including open-source projects that we customise or extend.

  • Build HTTP, REST, and gRPC service interfaces used by internal engineering teams.

  • Write meaningful unit and integration tests, and treat testability as a design property rather than an afterthought.

Reliability and Production Operations:

  • Lead incident response for platform-level issues; investigate root causes and author postmortems that result in durable fixes.

  • Troubleshoot production systems using logs, metrics, traces, and profiling tools.

  • Diagnose and resolve performance and reliability problems across distributed systems.

  • Define and drive SLOs, and build the alerting that makes them actionable.

Infrastructure as Code and Delivery:

  • Own infrastructure as code across the platform, authoring reusable modules and maintaining them as the platform evolves.

  • Build and improve CI/CD and GitOps delivery workflows so that teams can ship safely and frequently.

  • Balance developer velocity against reliability, security, and compliance requirements.

  • Plan and execute cloud migration initiatives, including moving production workloads between cloud providers or environments while maintaining reliability and minimizing downtime.

Observability:

  • Build and maintain metrics, dashboards, alerting policies, and distributed tracing.

  • Instrument services so that failures are diagnosable without a code change.

Collaboration:

  • Partner with product, security, and infrastructure teams to gather requirements and align on architecture.

  • Contribute to design reviews and help set technical direction.

  • Mentor other engineers and raise the standard of engineering practice around you.

Qualifications:

Education and Experience:

  • 6+ years of professional experience in software, platform, infrastructure, or site reliability engineering, including significant time operating production distributed systems.

  • Demonstrated experience building and operating production Kubernetes platforms, not only deploying onto them.

  • Production experience writing Go, Python or Java.

  • Experience designing systems from an ambiguous starting point and carrying them to production.

  • Experience migrating cloud services, including planning and executing moves of production workloads between providers or environments.

  • Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Technical Skills:

  • Strong understanding of Kubernetes internals: networking (CNI), NetworkPolicy, resource management, and cluster behaviour under load.

  • Hands-on experience with a service mesh (Istio, Envoy, Linkerd, or similar) and with mTLS and workload identity.

  • Solid Linux fundamentals, including cgroups and resource management.

  • Infrastructure as code at scale, Terraform or an equivalent.

  • Production experience with at least one major cloud platform (GCP, AWS, or Azure); multi-cloud experience is a strong plus.

  • Observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, and query languages such as PromQL.

  • Production experience with relational databases, including PostgreSQL or managed Postgres-compatible services, and an understanding of their replication and failover characteristics.

  • Docker and container tooling as part of the delivery lifecycle.

  • Strong debugging and performance profiling skills.

Preferred:

  • Experience with Go testing frameworks such as Ginkgo and Gomega.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager, Medical & Health Sciences Education
jobs.excerpt: Partner with the Higher Education Programs Preparing Tomorrow’s Healthcare Professionals.
jobs.description:
Partner with the Higher Education Programs Preparing Tomorrow’s Healthcare Professionals.

The best customer relationships begin with trust: understanding what a partner is trying to achieve, helping them work through difficult challenges, and showing up with insight when it matters.

At Acuity Insights, those conversations happen in a uniquely meaningful context. We partner with medical and health sciences programs as they educate and develop the people who will become tomorrow’s healthcare professionals. Our Program Experience products help institutions manage complex academic programs, understand their data, and support learners throughout their journey.

As our next Customer Success Manager, you’ll build trusted partnerships with program leaders, educators, and administrators, helping them realize meaningful value from Acuity’s products while uncovering new opportunities to deepen those relationships over time.

This is a Customer Success role where helping customers realize long-term value naturally leads to renewals, growth, and lasting partnerships. Our strongest partnerships grow because customers trust our guidance, see meaningful outcomes, and choose to deepen their relationship with us over time.

You’ll also join at an important moment for our Customer Success team. We’re creating greater focus between Customer Success, Implementation, and Support so our CSMs can spend more of their time understanding their partners, strengthening relationships, driving value, and identifying opportunities for growth. The foundations are already here. You’ll have the opportunity to help shape what comes next.

If you enjoy becoming deeply invested in your customers’ success, developing a point of view about what will help them get there, and turning that understanding into trusted partnerships and meaningful growth, you’ll find a lot to dig into here.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in Canada.

Before you apply: Thoughtful use of AI is welcome. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out.

The Work You’ll Do

In your first few weeks, you’ll immerse yourself in our customers’ world. You’ll learn how medical and health sciences programs operate, get to know the institutions in your portfolio, and build your understanding of our Program Experience products: One45, Analytics, and MSPE Builder.

You’ll gradually take ownership of a focused portfolio of institutional partners, spanning a mix of mid-sized and strategic relationships. The portfolio is designed to give you the space to understand your customers deeply, build relationships across stakeholders, and take meaningful ownership of their success. You’ll have experienced teammates and specialized teams across Acuity to draw on as you build your product and domain expertise.

As you take ownership of your portfolio, you’ll:

Build relationships that go beyond the day-to-day.
Understand what matters to each partner, where they’re trying to go, and what may be getting in the way. You’ll work with programs ranging from established institutions with complex stakeholder environments to newer programs looking for more guidance.

Own the relationship, not every task.
Stay accountable for the partner and their outcomes while bringing in expertise from Implementation, Support, Product, Sales, and other teams when it’s needed.

Drive retention and uncover opportunities for growth.
Understand account health, anticipate risk, and identify where greater adoption or another Acuity solution could create meaningful value. When an opportunity is qualified, you’ll partner with Sales to move it forward.

Bring customer insight back into Acuity.
Look across your portfolio for patterns, challenges, and opportunities that can help Product, Sales, and other teams make better decisions.

Help shape how Customer Success works.
Look beyond your own portfolio for ways to improve how we manage customers, collaborate across teams, and use AI and other tools to make Customer Success more proactive and scalable.

Most of our Program Experience partners are in North America, with a significant concentration in the United States and a growing international footprint. Most of your work will happen remotely, with occasional opportunities to meet partners through campus visits, conferences, and industry events.

What You’ll Help Make Possible

The relationships you build will have an impact far beyond your own portfolio. You’ll help medical and health sciences programs get more value from their partnership with Acuity while contributing directly to our growth.

Build partnerships customers want to grow.
Develop trusted, long-term relationships that help institutions achieve meaningful outcomes and continue choosing Acuity year after year.

Help customers solve bigger challenges.
Understand what your partners are trying to accomplish and develop a point of view about how Acuity can help. Connect them with the products, insights, and expertise that move them toward their goals rather than simply responding to the request in front of you.

Spot opportunities to create more value.
Help partners get greater value from the solutions they use today and identify where other Acuity capabilities could help them solve new problems.

Bring the voice of the customer into Acuity.
Turn what you’re hearing across your portfolio into insight that can inform better products, stronger customer experiences, and smarter business decisions.

Help define the next chapter of Customer Success.
Contribute ideas and improve how the team works together as we build a more strategic, commercially accountable, and customer-centered CS function.

The impact of your work will be visible in stronger customer relationships, healthier renewals, meaningful commercial growth, and institutions that continue choosing Acuity as a trusted partner. Behind those outcomes are medical and health sciences programs preparing people for careers that have a profound impact on the communities they serve.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role isn’t about quick wins. It’s about earning trust, developing judgment, creating momentum, and delivering meaningful outcomes for both your customers and the business.

In your first few months, you’ll build your understanding of our products, customers, and the medical and health sciences education environment while beginning to take ownership of customer relationships. There’s meaningful domain and product knowledge to learn, and you’ll have support from experienced teammates as you build confidence.

As you ramp, you’ll establish strong relationships across your accounts and develop healthy rhythms around customer engagement, renewal readiness, account health, and portfolio planning. You’ll increasingly know when to advise directly and when bringing in specialized expertise will create a better customer outcome.

By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted advisor to your customers, confidently leading strategic conversations and contributing directly to retention and revenue growth. Your customers will know they can count on you, and your teammates will value the perspective and insight you bring back from your portfolio.

Who You’ll Work With

You’ll report to our Senior Manager, Customer Success (Program Experience), joining a close-knit team with deep knowledge of our customers, products, and the medical and health sciences environment.

Customer Success is deeply collaborative at Acuity. You’ll maintain ownership of the partner relationship while working closely with specialized teams across the business:

Implementation, who lead onboarding, configuration, and implementation while you maintain customer context and relationship continuity.

Support, who provide specialized issue resolution while you stay connected to anything affecting the health of the relationship.

Sales, to align on account strategy, renewals, and qualified growth opportunities.

Product, to bring customer challenges, patterns, and context into product conversations.

Some of your biggest contributions will come from connecting the dots: understanding what matters to the customer, bringing the right people together, and helping Acuity see patterns and opportunities beyond a single account.

How You’ll Succeed Here

There’s no single profile for success in this role. But the people who thrive here tend to be curious, thoughtful, strategically minded, and genuinely invested in helping their customers succeed.

You stay curious.
You want to understand the problems your customers are trying to solve, not just the products they use. You ask thoughtful questions, connect the dots, and look beyond the immediate request to understand what matters most. When you spot a problem, you think about what could solve it, and whether there’s something others could learn from it too.

You build expertise.
You enjoy learning. Whether it’s our products, medical and health sciences education, or the higher education landscape, you know the best customer conversations are grounded in deep understanding.

You take ownership.
You see your portfolio as something you own, not something you manage. When something is unclear or evolving, you move work forward, follow through, and stay engaged until there’s a clear outcome.

You communicate with clarity and confidence.
You’re thoughtful, direct, and comfortable having difficult conversations when needed. You create clarity, build trust, and help people move forward together.

You thrive in change.
You’re comfortable in an evolving environment, adapt when priorities shift, and use new tools, including AI, thoughtfully to work more effectively and better support your customers.

You balance customer success with commercial thinking.
You understand that strong customer relationships and strong business outcomes go hand in hand. You’re comfortable leading renewal conversations, identifying growth opportunities, and helping customers invest where they’ll see genuine value.

Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running

There’s no single path into this role, and we don’t believe great Customer Success talent is measured by years of experience alone. What matters most is that you’ve built customer relationships, taken ownership of outcomes, and learned from those experiences.

You’ll likely bring experience in:

  • Customer Success, account management, consulting, or another customer-facing role where you’ve independently owned customer relationships or a portfolio.
  • Building trusted relationships across multiple stakeholders in complex customer organizations.
  • Supporting customer adoption, retention, and renewals while balancing customer value with business outcomes.
  • Identifying customer needs and opportunities where additional products, services, or expertise could create value.
  • Navigating challenging conversations and ambiguity with sound judgment and confidence.
  • Using CRM or Customer Success platforms such as Salesforce, ChurnZero, or similar tools.
  • Working independently in a remote environment with a high degree of ownership and initiative.
  • Supporting customers across North American time zones.

Experience in higher education, healthcare education, or complex B2B SaaS environments may help you ramp more quickly, but it isn’t required. We care more about your ability to learn, build trust, think critically, and take ownership.

If you’re earlier in your Customer Success career but have demonstrated exceptional curiosity, ownership, and a track record of building trusted customer relationships, we’d still love to hear from you.

How We Support You

  • Transparent compensation. A base salary between $78,000 - $85,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.
  • Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening technical skills, building confidence, or exploring new areas of interest.
  • Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.
  • Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.
  • Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.
  • Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.
  • Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.
  • Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully. Whether you apply directly, are referred, or connect through a recruiter or hiring manager, you’ll receive equal consideration.

We don’t use AI to evaluate applications, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements (e.g. Canadian residency and valid work authorization). In some of our conversations, AI may help with note-taking, but all evaluations and decisions are made by real humans.

Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you.

Steps in the Process

Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks from initial conversation to final decision.

  • Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.
  • Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.
  • Hiring Manager Conversation. A conversation about how you build trusted customer relationships, navigate ambiguity, and balance customer outcomes with commercial success. You’ll also have the opportunity to learn more about the evolution of Customer Success at Acuity, the portfolio you’ll support, and the challenges we’re working to solve alongside our partners.
  • Team Conversations. You’ll meet members of our Customer Success and Growth Enablement & Execution teams to explore how we work together across the customer journey. It’s also an opportunity for you to ask questions, get to know future teammates, and see what it would be like to work together day to day.
  • Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.
  • Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 130+ people who care deeply about our work and about each other. We want Acuity to be a place where people can do meaningful work, have room to grow, and build careers that are sustainable over time.

We put a lot of trust in people to own their work, make good decisions, and manage their time in ways that work for them and their teams. Being remote means we’re thoughtful about how we communicate and collaborate, creating space for focused work while making time to connect when it matters.

Day to day, that looks like:

  • High trust and autonomy in how work gets done
  • Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team
  • Space for deep work, balanced with intentional moments of connection
  • Curiosity, care, and people who are willing to help each other

That approach has earned Acuity recognition as one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers, an award that considers workplace culture, employee wellness, and people practices.

As Acuity grows and changes, we keep paying attention to how it feels to work here and making deliberate choices to protect what works while continuing to make it better.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights grew out of two separate challenges inside Canadian medical education.

One45 began at the University of British Columbia in the early 2000s, where educators were looking for a better way to manage the complex work of medical training. A few years later at McMaster University, researchers began exploring how admissions teams could understand more about applicants than grades and test scores alone. That work became Casper.

Those two paths came together in 2021. Today, Acuity builds products that support higher education institutions across more of the learner journey, from admissions and assessment through to program management, insight, and learner development.

Our work is still grounded in the same approach that shaped those early beginnings: start with a real problem, understand it deeply, and use research and technology thoughtfully to build something better.

Today, we continue to modernize our products, invest in research and innovation, and explore new ways to help institutions better understand and support human potential.

jobs.excerpt: Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions is seeking a Senior Solutions Analyst to join our Software Portfolio and Product organization, with a primary focus on supporting retail customers and opportunities throughout Latin America.
jobs.description:
Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions is seeking a Senior Solutions Analyst to join our Software Portfolio and Product organization, with a primary focus on supporting retail customers and opportunities throughout Latin America.

The Senior Solutions Analyst will help retailers navigate the complex journey from their existing retail technology landscape to Toshiba’s ELERA Commerce Platform and broader solution portfolio. This role will work directly with retailers to understand their current business operations, technology ecosystem, strategic priorities, and transformation objectives and develop pragmatic recommendations for how Toshiba can help them move forward.

This is a highly customer-facing and cross-functional role. The Senior Solutions Analyst will regularly collaborate with retailers, Sales, Product and Portfolio Management, Engineering, Professional Services, Business Analysts, business partners, solution providers, and systems integrators. The individual will be expected to independently lead customer conversations and discovery activities, formulate and defend recommendations, and then engage the appropriate domain experts to validate, refine, and ultimately execute the proposed solution.

This role will primarily support Toshiba’s business and customers throughout Latin Americabut may also support strategic customer engagements and initiatives in the United States and other markets as needed.

Responsibilities

  • Lead customer-facing discovery sessions, workshops, and strategic discussions to understand a retailer’s current business operations, technology landscape, challenges, priorities, and transformation objectives.
  • Assess complex retail environments encompassing Point of Sale (POS), payments, integrations, data flows, infrastructure, peripherals, cloud technologies, third-party applications, business processes, and other components of the retailer’s solution ecosystem.
  • Develop initial current-state and future-state solution assessments that provide a comprehensive view of the retailer’s existing landscape, major gaps, dependencies, opportunities, and potential paths toward Toshiba solutions.
  • Formulate and present clear, prescriptive recommendations for retailer transformation, balancing immediate business value with the retailer’s longer-term strategic objectives.
  • Identify pragmatic, incremental adoption strategies that deliver quick wins and early return on investment while establishing a foundation for broader transformation, avoiding unnecessary cost, complexity, and disruption associated with an all-at-once approach.
  • Evaluate alternative solution approaches based on business value, implementation effort, complexity, risk, dependencies, cost magnitude, time-to-value, and expected return on investment.
  • Translate complex business and technical considerations into recommendations that can be understood by retailer executives, business stakeholders, technical teams, Sales, and internal Toshiba organizations.
  • Support pre-sales activities, customer pursuits, solution positioning, and strategic account discussions by helping customers understand how Toshiba capabilities can address their business objectives.
  • Develop initial solution and transformation blueprints and then engage Product, Engineering, Architecture, Professional Services, Business Analysts, and other subject matter experts to validate assumptions and mature recommendations into executable plans.
  • Develop a strong working knowledge of the ELERA Commerce Platform and Toshiba’s broader retail solution portfolio after joining the organization, leveraging existing retail technology expertise to rapidly become an effective solution advisor.
  • Incorporate AI into regular working practices for research, analysis, synthesis, solution exploration, documentation, content creation, and reporting. Actively explore questions, test assumptions, alternatives, and challenge generated conclusions before incorporating AI-generated information into recommendations.
  • Travel up to 25% to support customer engagements, workshops, strategic pursuits, partner activities, and other business needs.

Required Skills

  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience in retail technology, retail software, solution consulting, business analysis, product management, professional services, solution strategy, systems integration, or a related discipline.
  • Significant hands-on experience working with retail Point of Sale (POS) software platforms and associated retail technologies.
  • Experience working with retailers in Latin America and an understanding of the operational and technology considerations associated with the region.
  • Professional fluency in Spanish and English, including the ability to lead customer workshops, deliver presentations, facilitate complex discussions, and communicate effectively with both business and technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead customer-facing discovery sessions, workshops, and solution discussions.
  • Strong understanding of retail operations and the role technology plays across the store and broader retail enterprise.
  • Broad technical literacy across areas such as system integrations, APIs, payments, data flows, infrastructure, cloud technologies, POS peripherals, enterprise applications, and related retail technology domains.
  • Exceptional analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize incomplete or complex information into actionable recommendations.
  • Strong understanding of business value and commercial considerations, including the ability to distinguish relative cost and effort, evaluate implementation tradeoffs, and discuss immediate, delayed, and recurring return on investment.
  • Strong facilitation and interpersonal skills with the ability to establish credibility and trusted-advisor relationships with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders.
  • Self-driven and comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy. Strong sense of ownership and accountability for the quality of analysis and customer outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability and motivation to incorporate AI into regular professional workflows, particularly for research, analysis, synthesis, exploration, content development, and reporting.
  • Strong judgment when working with AI-generated information, including the ability to question assumptions, validate conclusions, recognize limitations, and combine AI-assisted analysis with human expertise and independent critical thinking.

Preferred Skills

  • Deep experience with retail operations and retail technology environments throughout Latin America.
  • Detailed understanding of regional differences in retail operations, including fiscal and regulatory requirements, taxation, payments, localization, infrastructure, connectivity, labor and operational practices, and other market-specific considerations.
  • Experience working with Latin American retailers, regional business partners, technology providers, solution providers, and systems integrators.
  • Experience supporting large or complex retail transformation and modernization programs.
  • Experience developing current-state assessments, capability maps, fit-gap analyses, solution blueprints, transformations, or similar strategic deliverables.
  • Experience working with global retailers or supporting retail technology programs across multiple countries or regions.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

About the Company

Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions is a dynamic billion-dollar global company based in Research Triangle Park, NC, providing retail store solutions to your favorite brands. Have you ever been in a hurry and made use of the self-checkout at Lowe’s Foods, earned fuel rewards at Kroger, or just paid for purchases at retailers such as Walmart, Michaels, Carrefour, The Gap, Calvin Klein, Boots, BJ’s, or Costco? These are just a few examples of our in-store solutions and impressive customer base that made us the world’s installed market share leader.

EEO

We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Position Summary

We are seeking talented, committed and entrepreneurial individuals to join our Primary Market Research (PMR) practice area as Consultants. In general, Consultants at Trinity work as integral parts of one or more project teams comprised of skilled colleagues and management team members. This environment provides Consultants with exposure to a wide variety of strategic business issues, as well as the opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge of the life sciences industry. In this role, Consultants support with the development of robust strategic solutions for clients, spanning both qualitative and quantitative PMR projects and responsibilities. On each project, Consultants help develop research materials (discussion guides, screening criteria, surveys, stimuli, etc.) to address our clients’ key business questions, work closely with internal stakeholders and external partners to launch surveys and field interviews, analyze and interpret PMR data, and present findings to project teams and clients. Their work is the base upon which our recommendations are ultimately grounded. Consultants develop their skills through undergoing comprehensive formal and informal training, as well as receiving mentorship that encourages them to stretch their skills.

Essential Functions

  • Draft materials for research (discussion guides, surveys, stimuli, etc.) to help address our clients’ key business questions

  • Manage / Work closely with programming and fielding partners

  • Analyze quantitative and qualitative primary market research data to address the business objectives

  • Develop a highly visual and compelling PowerPoint presentation of the “story” and implications for our clients

  • Add value by translating research findings into the “so-whats” for our clients

  • Aid in proposal development as needed

  • Mentor Associate Consultants and new Consultant hires

Position Requirements

Education: Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in market research, engineering, pharmacy, medicine, or health sciences disciplines, or related fields at a top tier university; demonstrated interest in the life sciences field is a plus. Graduate training (Masters/Doctoral degree) in STEM fields strongly preferred.

Work Experience: 3-5 years of experience in primary market research, consulting or other relevant areas within the life sciences industry. Experience with both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies strongly preferred.

Other Skills:

  • Demonstrated quantitative and analytical skills

  • Strong problem solving and logical thinking skills

  • Ability to interpret and run statistical analysis is preferred

  • Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint

  • Familiarity with secondary datasets

  • Excellent communication in English (written and verbal) and interpersonal relations skills

  • Ability to manage time and work on multiple projects concurrently

  • Desire and ability to work in a dynamic, fast-paced environment

  • Ability to manage work independently with guidance from team leaders in the US

Trinity powers the future of life sciences commercialization through the fusion of human and artificial intelligence. By blending deep therapeutic expertise and trusted human ingenuity with a purpose-built technology platform, Trinity accelerates clarity and confidence at every step of the commercialization journey—from pre-launch to scale to loss of exclusivity. For more than 30 years, the world’s leading pharmaceutical, biotech, and medtech companies have relied on Trinity’s foresight, execution, and partnership to deliver confident product launches, decisive market advantage, and measurable patient impact. During that time, Trinity expanded from its first office in Waltham, MA to 1,300 professionals across 14 offices and five continents, setting new industry standards in quality, responsiveness, and client partnership. Executive Assistant (EA) – Calendar, Travel & Executive Support | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours (Flexibility Required)

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a high-performing Executive Assistant (EA) to support senior leadership in a fast-paced, high-accountability environment.

This is more than a traditional administrative role. You’ll serve as a trusted executive support partner, helping leadership stay focused on high-impact priorities while ensuring calendars, communication, meetings, travel, follow-ups, and operational details run smoothly behind the scenes.

You’ll take ownership of complex scheduling, executive communication, meeting preparation, travel logistics, and priority tracking while anticipating needs and ensuring important details never fall through the cracks.

If you’re proactive, highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable supporting senior executives in a fast-moving environment, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

Executive Calendar & Scheduling Management

  • Manage complex executive calendars across multiple time zones
  • Coordinate meetings, calls, travel, and competing scheduling priorities
  • Resolve calendar conflicts proactively
  • Optimize executive schedules to protect time for high-priority work
  • Coordinate internal and external meetings efficiently
  • Use tools such as:
    • Google Calendar
    • Microsoft Outlook
    • Calendly
    • Other scheduling platforms

Executive Communication & Inbox Support

  • Draft, proofread, and send professional emails and communications
  • Manage executive inboxes and prioritize important requests
  • Screen calls, messages, and meeting requests
  • Identify urgent matters requiring executive attention
  • Maintain professional and timely communication with stakeholders
  • Act as a liaison between executives, clients, and internal teams

Meeting Preparation & Follow-Up

  • Prepare agendas, briefing notes, talking points, and meeting materials

  • Ensure executives are properly prepared for upcoming conversations
  • Take meeting notes and document key decisions
  • Track action items, owners, and deadlines
  • Follow up with stakeholders to ensure commitments are completed

Travel & Logistics Coordination

  • Coordinate domestic and international travel
  • Book flights, hotels, transportation, and other arrangements
  • Prepare clear and organized travel itineraries
  • Coordinate travel schedules with executive calendars
  • Manage last-minute changes and scheduling adjustments
  • Track travel expenses and support reimbursements

Executive Priorities & Project Support

  • Track executive priorities, projects, and ongoing initiatives
  • Maintain visibility into deadlines and outstanding deliverables
  • Follow up with teams to keep projects moving
  • Help executives stay aligned on commitments and next steps
  • Conduct research and prepare reports or summaries
  • Support operational and administrative projects as needed

Documentation & Administrative Operations

  • Maintain organized digital filing systems and documentation
  • Prepare and format reports, presentations, and business materials
  • Organize executive information for quick access
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation
  • Handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion

Requirements

  • 3+ years of Executive Assistant or senior administrative support experience
  • Experience directly supporting executives in fast-paced environments
  • Strong calendar management and scheduling experience across multiple time zones
  • Strong experience coordinating meetings and executive priorities
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication
  • High attention to detail and organizational ability
  • Strong time-management and prioritization skills
  • Ability to manage multiple requests and changing priorities simultaneously
  • Ability to handle confidential information professionally and discreetly
  • Comfortable working independently with limited supervision
  • Ability to work during U.S. client business hours with flexibility when required

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in:
    • Startups
    • Agencies
    • Consulting firms
    • High-growth companies
  • Familiarity with:
    • Slack
    • Zoom
    • Notion
    • Asana
    • Similar collaboration and project-management tools
  • Experience supporting multiple executives simultaneously
  • Experience coordinating complex domestic and international travel
  • Exposure to operations, project coordination, or broader business support workflows

Tools & Platforms

Google Workspace | Google Calendar | Microsoft Office | Microsoft Outlook | Calendly | Slack | Zoom | Notion | Asana | Collaboration & Scheduling Tools

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

  • Anticipate executive needs instead of waiting for instructions
  • Can confidently manage a complex and constantly changing calendar
  • Naturally create structure in fast-moving environments
  • Communicate professionally with executives, clients, and internal teams
  • Follow up consistently and ensure commitments are completed
  • Remain calm when schedules or priorities change unexpectedly
  • Have exceptional attention to detail
  • Understand how to prioritize urgent versus important requests
  • Exercise good judgment with confidential information
  • Take ownership from assignment through completion

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You may start your day by reviewing executive calendars, preparing briefing notes, checking inbox priorities, and confirming the day’s meetings and logistics.

Throughout the day, you’ll manage scheduling requests, coordinate meetings, prepare agendas and materials, handle executive communications, organize travel, and track follow-ups.

You may also check project updates, follow up with teams on outstanding deliverables, conduct research, prepare reports, and organize the executive’s schedule for the following day.

In short: you ensure executives operate with maximum efficiency, organization, and clarity.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Calendar accuracy and scheduling efficiency
  • Reduction in scheduling conflicts and administrative delays
  • Timely communication and follow-up execution
  • Completion of meeting action items
  • Smooth travel and logistics coordination
  • Accuracy and quality of executive materials
  • Effective tracking of executive priorities
  • Executive satisfaction and overall support quality

Why This Role Stands Out

  • High-visibility role supporting senior leadership directly
  • Opportunity to work closely with executives and decision-makers
  • Exposure to executive operations and business priorities
  • Fast-paced, professional, and growth-oriented environment
  • Opportunity to develop broader operational and project-management skills
  • Potential career progression into:
    • Senior Executive Assistant
    • Operations
    • Project Management
    • Chief of Staff pathways

Interview Process

  1. Initial Application
  2. Spark Hire One-Way Video Interview
  3. Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter

As part of the application process, all candidates are required to complete a one-way video interview through Spark Hire.

After completing the first step of your application, you’ll receive a Spark Hire invitation by email with instructions to record and submit your video responses.

Completion of the Spark Hire video is required to be considered for the next stage. Please check your inbox as well as your spam or junk folder for the invitation.

Apply Now

If you have strong experience in executive support, complex calendar management, travel coordination, executive communication, and priority management, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and help senior leadership operate more efficiently by keeping their schedules, communication, logistics, and priorities organized and moving forward.

jobs.description:
Sunday
Director of Engineering
Full-time · Reports to CEO/Leadership Team · Boulder, CO or Remote

About the Role

Sunday is looking for a Director of Engineering to lead and elevate a talented, close-knit engineering team through a pivotal moment. We're building something novel in the lawn care category, not reinventing an existing category, and our engineers are energized by that focus. This role exists to protect and grow that momentum: setting technical vision, building org-level capability, and bringing in an AI focus.
This is a hands-on leadership role with real strategic ownership. You'll need to be credible in the weeds, able to understand what's happening in the codebase and the business, while also sitting close to company leadership, translating company vision into an engineering roadmap, and making the structural calls the team doesn't have bandwidth to make themselves.
Above all, we need a builder. Someone who gets genuinely excited about writing code and shipping products, not solely a people manager. You'll rally the team by being in it with them, and you'll partner directly with Product as a true collaborator, not an order-taker: we need someone who understands how product and engineering decisions shape each other.

Vision & Strategy

  • Develop a technical vision for engineering that ties directly to Sunday's business goals, and translate it into a 6–12 month roadmap built with Product and the Leadership Team
  • Build and own Sunday's AI strategy for engineering, establish a consistent approach to AI-assisted and agentic development, and use it to help the team move faster and fail faster
  • Serve as the connective layer between business/product priorities and the engineering team

AI-Native Product Direction

  • Push Sunday toward becoming a genuinely AI-native product company, not a deterministic product with a chatbot bolted on, but one where core functionality is LLM-driven where it makes sense
  • Bring real excitement and a point of view about this shift, and get the team energized about building toward it together
  • Support early agent-based project work and help set a broader, more consistent direction for how the team builds and evaluates agentic systems
  • Establish evaluation practices (evals) for AI-driven functionality; fluency with eval tooling (e.g., Braintrust, Langfuse, or similar) is a strong plus, since non-deterministic, LLM-driven logic can't be tested the way traditional deterministic code is

Technical Maturity & Architecture

  • Bring maturity to foundational infrastructure and architecture decisions
  • Identify and invest in the technical decisions that save the team time now, rather than accumulating further shortcuts
  • Bring a builder's mindset to this work personally; this isn't a hands-off architecture review function; it's active, credible participation in solving it

Org Building & Talent

  • Own hiring strategy and interview process for both ICs and future managers, partnering closely with the People team; instill and maintain a high hiring bar
  • Prevent single points of failure, put institutional knowledge, documentation, and cross-training in place
  • Give engineers real paths to grow, including mentorship, stretch opportunities, and regular, honest development feedback

Execution & Delivery

  • Hold the team accountable to its own goals; regularly evaluate team structure and workflow to keep the org moving quickly
  • Codify and disseminate engineering best practices, testing, code review, PR norms, and how those practices scale as AI-assisted development increases velocity, so speed doesn't outpace quality
  • Own engineering metrics — delivery against roadmap, quality/bug backlog, system performance and uptime, and team velocity, and use them to surface bottlenecks to leadership
  • Deliver honest, frequent, and respectful feedback, and build a culture where the team gives and receives it the same way

Cross-Functional Leadership & Product Partnership

  • Represent engineering as part of company leadership, communicate plans, tradeoffs, and challenges to other functional heads in terms the whole business can act on
  • Act as a true product partner given how much of Sunday's product is (and will increasingly be) LLM-driven; engineering and product decisions are directly intertwined, not sequential handoffs
  • Understand how product thinks, and bring engineering's perspective into product conversations early — this is a collaboration, not a request queue

What Success Looks Like

  • The team feels led, not managed, with clear priorities, cleared blockers, and visible follow-through
  • Strong opinions, held loosely: you set direction but trust engineers to own execution
  • The team has real conviction that engineering is heading in the right direction
  • A working AI strategy the whole team is aligned on, with visible gains in velocity and quality

What You Bring

  • Proven experience leading engineering at a small-to-mid-size or growth-stage company, with a track record of taking on increasing scope
  • A genuine builder, you want to be hands-on writing code and shaping product, not solely managing people and process
  • Strong individual technical credibility — you can go deep enough to earn trust with senior engineers, not just manage from a distance
  • Direct experience with, or strong enthusiasm for, AI-native product development — building products where core functionality is LLM-driven rather than deterministic, not just adding an AI chat feature to an existing product
  • Familiarity with LLM evaluation practices and tooling (Braintrust, Langfuse, or similar), given the shift toward non-deterministic, AI-driven functionality
  • Front-end depth, or demonstrated ability to grow it across a team
  • Hands-on familiarity with AI-assisted and agentic development workflows, and a clear point of view on how to scale them responsibly
  • A naturally curious, learning-oriented mindset, hungry to keep growing and to bring the team along with you
  • Experience building org structure, hiring processes, and team practices from a lighter-weight or informal state
  • A true product-collaboration mindset: understands how product and engineering decisions shape each other, and doesn't need — or want — a roadmap simply handed to them
  • A business-minded, collaborative style, comfortable building relationships across the whole company, not just within engineering
  • Humility and directness, able to talk openly about mistakes and how they were resolved, and to give feedback as a gift
  • A communicator who can move fluidly between technical depth and company-wide clarity

A Note on Team Culture

Sunday's engineering team values being in the weeds together, moving quickly, and staying focused on one clear, differentiated product direction. We're looking for a leader who amplifies that — someone the team describes the way they describe their best examples of leadership: present, communicative, and unafraid to tackle the hard stuff directly.

As a company rooted in nature, we deeply understand the benefits of diversity. We work to build a culture that attracts a diverse mix of talented people to help us bring lawn care out of the dark ages. We are committed to building a diverse, vibrant team that brings determination and passion to our work everyday.

1. INTRODUCTION

SHAPE and the NCI Agency are jointly delivering the Alliance Persistent Surveillance from Space Programme. This programme serves NATO and the nations and presents an opportunity to enhance and accelerate situational awareness and decision making through a dedicated programme for the access to shared space data and the integration of the data into NATO systems. Through pioneering the ability of the Alliance to harness space capabilities and deliver operational effect from the Space Domain, this proposal will deliver a step change in the Alliance ability to remain informed through access to Space data.

2. SCOPE OF WORK

Under the direction of the NCI Agency, the incumbent will perform duties to include the following:

Collection Tool Data Integration: Managing ACO requirements for APSS commercial data integration.

Collection Tool User Interface Management: Supporting ACO requests and investigating/implementing changes to user interface.

System Troubleshooting: Investigating and resolving data flow bottlenecks and technical issues in production environments.

Collaboration & Documentation: Working with cross-functional teams to define requirements and maintaining documentation for the APSS Collection Tool.

Acceptance Criteria A3: Accepted periodic report satisfying the KPI and Acceptance Criteria framework set out below.

Acceptance Criteria A4: Accepted periodic report satisfying the KPI and Acceptance Criteria framework set out below.

Deliverable D5: Document Collection Tool status report for Reporting Period 5 (Option Year 2027), covering operational and technical status; issues arising or handled during the period; service and collection metrics; and risks, actions, and recommendations.

Acceptance Criteria A5: Accepted periodic report satisfying the KPI and Acceptance Criteria framework set out below.

Deliverable D6: Document Collection Tool status report for Reporting Period 6 (Option Year 2027), covering operational and technical status; issues arising or handled during the period; service and collection metrics; and risks, actions, and recommendations.

Acceptance Criteria A6: Accepted periodic report satisfying the KPI and Acceptance Criteria framework set out below.

Deliverable D7: Document Collection Tool status report for Reporting Period 7 (Option Year 2027), including a consolidated six-period trend assessment, covering operational and technical status; issues arising or handled during the period; service and collection metrics; and risks, actions, and recommendations.

Acceptance Criteria A7: Accepted final periodic report and consolidated seven-period analysis satisfying the KPI and Acceptance Criteria framework set out below.

Required Content of Each Deliverable (Deliverables D1–D7)

Each deliverable shall contain, as a minimum:

1. Executive summary and overall RAG status.

2. Availability and operational status of the Document Collection Tool.

3. Status of its components, interfaces, collectors, repositories, and scheduled jobs.

4. Issues opened, resolved, outstanding, or carried forward during the reporting period.
